title: Cursor Build Live Apps - From Prompt to Share Link
content:
Most apps you ask an agent to write never
leave localhost.
On 5 Nov 2026, Cursor shipped Build Live
Apps: CLOUD AGENTS can scaffold, host, and
share a live link from inside Cursor.
I use Cursor and Grok Bot every day, so
this is familiar territory — but I will
not invent a ship story or hours saved I
never measured.
Stay for the security checks and the
explicit publish step. That gate is the
product.
Verified from the Cursor changelog.
Kick off a cloud agent and tell it
explicitly that you want to build an app.
Cursor scaffolds the web app, spins up
Postgres if needed, sets authentication
behind Cursor SSO, and provisions hosting.
If the app needs secrets for your systems,
Cursor asks for them.
When you publish, you pick a UNIQUE DOMAIN
and get a live link back.
Available on all PAID PLANS with cloud
agents enabled. Origin and GitHub today.
GitLab support coming soon.
Controls and guardrails matter more than
the demo GIF.
When you publish, Cursor runs
DETERMINISTIC AND AGENTIC SECURITY CHECKS
— secrets in app files, exposed
credentials, common footguns.
If a check fails, the agent tells you what to fix.
Nothing goes live until the checks pass
AND you EXPLICITLY PUBLISH.
Team admins can see every app and every
secret. They can add rules, approve
publishes the review blocked, and
unpublish any app.
Share with specific people, groups, or the
whole team behind Cursor sign-in.
Individual plans can also share publicly.
Here is a walkthrough pattern. Say you
want an internal ops tool — event
registration or a simple pipeline
dashboard.
Step 1: start a cloud agent. Say out loud
that you want to build an app, not just a
local prototype.
Step 2: review the scaffold. Confirm
Postgres only if you need it. Confirm SSO
stays behind Cursor.
Step 3: read the security findings. Fix
secrets before you chase UI polish.
Step 4: pick a unique domain. Explicitly
publish. Then share to people or groups.
Imagine a sales desk that needs a seating
chart app by Friday. The agent can draft
it. You still own the publish tap.
That is a labelled hypothetical, not my
measured result.
Cursor says users across sales,
operations, legal, finance, and
engineering are already building internal
apps — ops tools, training experiences,
live dashboards, service portals.
The point for professionals: the
bottleneck moved from writing code to
deciding what is allowed to go live.
Admins who can see every app and secret
suddenly have a real control plane.
If you are evaluating this for a team,
enable cloud agents on a paid plan, write
a one-page publish policy, and treat
unpublish as a first-class runbook.
Here's my take.
Build Live Apps is not magic deploy. It is
scaffold plus hosting plus a hard publish
gate with security checks.
The skill that transfers: reading agent
diffs, clearing secret findings, and
keeping a human on the publish button.
I will not claim I cut a project from days
to minutes. I will claim the product shape
matches how serious teams should ship
agent-built tools.
Comment LIVE and I'll send you the Cursor
changelog link for Build Live Apps.
Follow for your daily AI update.
